correctness.rationale: For each rank-one T=f⊗x with a=f(x), T²=aT. If a=0 the square identity is trivial; if a≠0 then P=T/a is a rank-one projection and T²=a²P with a²>0. From the assumed equality at scale 1, the triangle inequality gives equality for every positive scalar t, separately on 0<t≤1 and t≥1. Thus the corresponding signed-square Daugavet identity holds for every rank-one T, and Langemets 2026 gives the Daugavet property for real dim X>1. The forward implication is immediate from the Daugavet equation applied to ±P.

value.rationale: The criterion materially simplifies how the Daugavet property can be tested: one fixed scalar identity on rank-one idempotents suffices, instead of checking an identity for squares of every rank-one operator. It also pinpoints the exact 1+||P|| strengthening of the classical bad-projections inequality that restores equivalence with Daugavet, giving a clean conceptual boundary between two established geometric notions.
